definition: A nonsense word that can mean cool, bad, or just random; it is also the name of a viral animated series where singing toilet heads battle camera-headed agents.
example: "That joke was so skibidi." "Skibidi what?" "Just skibidi."
exampleTranslation: That joke was so random and silly.
context: Used mostly as a joke word by kids; meaning shifts with context and often has none. Adults hear it as the poster child of brain rot.
origin: From the Skibidi Toilet YouTube animation series created by Alexey Gerasimov (DaFuq!?Boom!), which began in 2023; the sung phrase came from a remixed Bulgarian song clip.
mistakes: There is no fixed meaning; trying to define it too precisely misses the joke.

definition: A viral nonsense chant and hand gesture (palms up, alternating up and down) with no real meaning, shouted for the fun of it, especially when the number 67 comes up.
example: "What's the answer?" "Six seven!" "That is not even close."
exampleTranslation: "What's the answer?" "Just a silly chant!" "That is not even close."
context: Popular in schools in 2025; classes often shout it when a 6, a 7, or 67 appears, which frustrates teachers. Its meaninglessness is the point.
origin: Spread on TikTok and basketball edits, tied to a song and clips of a basketball player; reported to have exploded among kids in 2025. Dictionary.com reportedly named "6-7" its 2025 Word of the Year; verify before quoting.
mistakes: Do not look for a hidden meaning; asking "what does it mean?" is part of the joke.

definition: Describes a person (meme-ishly, a man) seen as independent, cool, and doing his own thing outside normal social ranks; now mostly used jokingly.
example: "He ate lunch alone and didn't care. Total sigma."
exampleTranslation: He ate lunch alone and didn't care. Very independent and cool.
context: Began as a serious "manosphere" personality label; kids today use it as a goofy compliment or a meme.
origin: From online self-help and "manosphere" ranking of male personalities (alpha, beta, sigma); later turned into a joke meme on TikTok.
sensitiveNote: The original alpha/beta/sigma hierarchy comes from online "manosphere" communities with sexist ideas; kids mostly use the word as a joke.

definition: A joking reaction of confusion or surprise, a swap of "sigma" into the phrase "what the heck."
exampleTranslation: What in the world is that?
context: Often delivered in a nerdy "erm" voice for comedy. Pure meme, rarely sincere.
origin: Brain rot remix of a mild swear phrase, spread on TikTok and YouTube.

definition: Taking a bite or some of a friend's food as a joking "tax" they have to pay.
plain: a bite stolen from a friend
exampleTranslation: Give me a fry. I get a share.
context: Used jokingly among friends over snacks and lunch; verb form "to fanum tax" is common.
origin: Named for streamer Fanum, a member of the AMP group, who was known for taking bites of his friends' food on stream.

definition: An invisible score of how cool, confident, or impressive someone is; people "gain" or "lose" aura points for their actions.
exampleTranslation: He caught the dropped tray. That was super cool.
context: Used to rate moments, usually jokingly, with big numbers. Gaining aura is cool; losing it is embarrassing.
origin: Popularized on TikTok and in gaming and streaming communities; builds on older ideas of a person's "aura" or vibe.

definition: Losing coolness points through an embarrassing or uncool moment.
exampleTranslation: He tripped on stage. How embarrassing.
context: Teasing, usually mild. Often scored with exaggerated numbers.

definition: Deliberately doing things to look effortlessly cool and rack up admiration.
example: "He walked in slow motion with sunglasses. Aura farming."
exampleTranslation: He walked in slow motion with sunglasses, trying to look cool.
context: Can be admiring or mocking. Went viral in 2025 through clips of young boat racers in Indonesia dancing at the front of a boat.
origin: Popularized in 2025 partly by a viral clip of a boy dancing on the prow of a Riau (Indonesia) racing boat, though the phrase builds on earlier "aura" slang.

definition: Used as a joke for anything weird, cursed, or chaotic; the U.S. state itself is the butt of the meme.
example: "The cat is in the fridge again. Only in Ohio."
exampleTranslation: The cat is in the fridge again. That is just weird.
context: Not actually about the state; people from Ohio often joke along. "Ohio final boss" means an absurdly strong or odd person.
origin: Grew from internet jokes about Ohio being strange or unremarkable, then exploded in Gen Alpha brain rot.

definition: An exclamation of shock or admiration, from "goddamn"; it began as a reaction to a person's curvy body, though many kids use it for any surprising thing.
exampleTranslation: You got a perfect score? Wow!
context: Pronounced like "GYAT." Used by kids who often don't know its body-focused origin. Teachers may ban it.
origin: Respelling of "goddamn," from streamer and Black internet communities, popularized in 2022–2023 reacting to women's bodies, then used generically.
sensitiveNote: Originated as a reaction to someone's body and is a respelling of "goddamn"; many kids use it as a general "wow" without knowing, but it can be objectifying.

definition: Pressing the tongue to the roof of the mouth in a trend that claims it sharpens the jawline; used jokingly to silence someone or show off a "chiseled" face.
exampleTranslation: Stop talking and pose for a sharper jaw.
context: Often a joke gesture (finger across lips) meant to tell someone to be quiet. Health claims are not scientifically established.
origin: Named after British orthodontist John Mew, whose "orthotropics" ideas about tongue posture and jaw shape went viral on TikTok.

definition: Trying to make yourself more attractive using grooming, fitness, and sometimes extreme methods.
example: "He started looksmaxxing with skincare and a haircut."
exampleTranslation: He started improving his looks with skincare and a haircut.
context: Ranges from healthy habits like skincare and exercise to harmful extremes. Sometimes mocked.
origin: Came from online self-improvement and incel-adjacent forums, then spread to TikTok as meme.
sensitiveNote: Rooted in online forums with appearance-obsessed and sometimes extreme communities; can promote unhealthy body image and risky "hacks."

definition: A suffix meaning to push something to the maximum, like "sleepmaxxing" or "studymaxxing."
exampleTranslation: I'm getting as much sleep as possible before the test.
context: Attach it to any habit; often jokey.
origin: Spun off from "looksmaxxing" in online forums.
mistakes: Using it for something negative reads as a joke, not a serious plan.

definition: To outshine someone, especially in looks or presence, so they seem lesser by comparison.
example: "He got mogged by the new kid."
exampleTranslation: He was outshone by the new kid.
context: Short for "AMOG" (alpha male of the group). Jokey in meme use but can sting.
origin: From the acronym AMOG on incel-adjacent forums; later spread through TikTok.
sensitiveNote: Comes from forum culture that ranks men by looks; can be used to put people down.

definition: A person who seems to act like a scripted background character with no independent thought, from video games' "non-player characters."
example: "He said the same line three times. Total NPC."
exampleTranslation: He repeated the same line three times, like a robot.
context: Used as a mild insult. Some find it dehumanizing.
origin: Gaming term for non-player characters, later turned into a political and social meme and then into TikTok NPC streaming.

definition: A TikTok live trend where streamers act like game NPCs, repeating odd phrases whenever viewers send gifts.
example: "She did NPC streaming with the ice cream line."
exampleTranslation: She acted like a game character on stream.
context: Became widely known in 2023; viewers tip small gifts to trigger the phrases.
origin: Popularized on TikTok Live in 2023 (the "ice cream so good" line was a famous example).

definition: Silly, low-effort online content and slang that people joke is turning their brains to mush; also the feeling from watching too much of it.
meanings: The internet-meme culture itself (e.g. "that is brain rot")
example: "I watched memes all day and now I have brain rot."
exampleTranslation: I watched memes all day and my brain feels numb.
context: Used by kids with pride and by adults with worry. Oxford University Press named "brain rot" its 2024 Word of the Year.
origin: The phrase appears as far back as Thoreau's Walden (1854), but exploded on social media around 2023–2024; Oxford chose it as Word of the Year 2024.

definition: "Goofy" plus "ahh" used as a playful descriptor meaning silly or ridiculous.
example: "That goofy ahh sound effect made me laugh."
exampleTranslation: That silly sound effect made me laugh.
context: The "ahh" is a stand-in for a rude word, but it is used as a harmless-sounding exaggeration. Often used with sound effects.
origin: From Black internet humor and TikTok, using stretched "ahh" in place of a rude word.
sensitiveNote: "Ahh" stands in for a rude word; kids often say it without that meaning, but adults may find it inappropriate.

definition: Someone with great charm, especially with crushes, now often joked about as a "master of rizz."
exampleTranslation: He is a master charmer.
context: Based on "rizz" (charisma). The "Rizzler" meme spread via a song about a kid who has strong charisma.
origin: Gen Alpha spin on "rizz" from the 2023 Skibidi-era meme scene, with a viral song using the line "Rizzler."

definition: Short for "delusional," used for people holding unrealistic hopes, often jokingly as self-confidence.
example: "I'm delulu about getting an A. Delulu is the solulu!"
exampleTranslation: I am overly hopeful about getting an A. Being hopeful is the solution!
context: Often a self-deprecating or empowering joke. "Delulu is the solulu" means a little delusion helps you succeed.
origin: From K-pop fan communities (fans delusional about idols), then mainstream on TikTok.

definition: To be desperately craving something, as in "I'm feining for snacks."
exampleTranslation: I'm craving pizza.
context: Spelled many ways; kids use it for any intense want.
origin: From "fiend," a person addicted to something, especially drugs; now used jokingly for any craving.
sensitiveNote: Origins are in drug-addiction language ("fiend"); kids use it lightly for cravings.

definition: To talk a lot, especially without saying much; a yapper is a very talkative person.
example: "He's been yapping about video games for an hour."
exampleTranslation: He has been talking about video games for an hour.
context: Mild tease. "Yap session" is a long chat; sometimes admired when a friend shares many stories.
origin: Existing word for noisy talk, revived by Gen Z and Alpha TikTok.

definition: Over-the-top praise for someone, usually undeserved; sucking up.
example: "Stop glazing him, he just made one basket."
exampleTranslation: Stop praising him too much, he just made one basket.
context: Used to tease friends who gush over a celebrity or each other.
origin: Linked to an adult slang phrase, likely from Black internet communities and sports fandom; kids may not know the origin.
sensitiveNote: Origin is sexual slang; many younger users treat it as simply "over-praising."

definition: Addressing an imaginary stream audience in everyday life, as if the speaker were livestreaming.
exampleTranslation: Everybody, I forgot my lunch again.
context: Spoken to friends or no one. Comes from streaming culture where "chat" is the viewers' message window.
origin: Twitch and streaming culture.

definition: A mock-serious question to an imaginary audience expressing disbelief.
example: "Chat, is this real? I got a seat on the bus."
exampleTranslation: Is this really happening? I got a seat on the bus.
context: Streamer-speak used for surprising or dramatic moments.
origin: Twitch and YouTube gaming culture.

definition: Asking an imaginary audience if you are in trouble or likely to fail.
example: "Chat, am I cooked? I haven't started the project."
exampleTranslation: Am I in trouble? I haven't started the project.
context: Often self-teasing, used before tests or deadlines.
origin: Streaming culture plus the Gen Z use of "cooked."

definition: A jokey label for someone who seems old, uncool, or out of touch.
example: "He still uses a flip phone. Unc status."
exampleTranslation: He still uses a flip phone. He is out of touch.
context: Short for "uncle." Usually a mild teasing; some people wear it as a badge.
origin: African American Vernacular English "unc" for an older guy, spread through memes and TikTok.

definition: A pet name for someone dear, such as a friend or sweetheart.
exampleTranslation: Hey dear, want to sit with us?
context: Warm and affectionate; used between friends and partners.
origin: Old pet name (from "pooh"), revived on TikTok.

definition: Friend or buddy, from British slang "blud," shortened from "blood" (brother); used jokingly as an address.
exampleTranslation: Buddy, that was incredible.
context: Used as a UK-flavored meme in the Gen Alpha corner of the internet. Playful, sometimes mocking.
origin: Black British and London slang, spread globally via memes and gaming.

definition: To lose your temper or make a rash decision when upset.
example: "He crashed out when he lost the game."
exampleTranslation: He had a meltdown when he lost the game.
context: Describes anger or a spiral, sometimes dramatic. Can be teasing.
origin: From Black internet and sports slang about a driver crashing; spread via TikTok.

definition: High praise for something excellent, funny, or perfectly made, as if it belonged in a great movie.
exampleTranslation: That ending was a masterpiece.
context: Can be sincere or ironic about silly things.
origin: From a meme of a Martin Scorsese-style praise, spread on Twitter and TikTok.

definition: A joke template listing odd things that arrived before the long-delayed game Grand Theft Auto VI.
example: "We got a new iPhone before GTA 6."
exampleTranslation: There has been a new iPhone and still no GTA 6.
context: Teases how long gamers have waited. Not related to content of the game.
origin: Gaming meme after GTA VI was officially confirmed in 2022 and its release was delayed.

definition: Being so awkward with a crush that you lower your charm instead of raising it.
example: "He gave a banana as a gift. Negative rizz."
exampleTranslation: He gave a banana as a gift. That was awkward.
context: Gen Alpha jokes about failed flirting.

definition: A jokey slur for robots and AI chatbots.
example: "I asked the clanker to do my homework."
exampleTranslation: I asked the AI to do my homework.
context: Went viral in 2025 as AI frustration meme; some note it echoes real slurs. Teachers may not appreciate cheating.
origin: From Star Wars (the Clone Wars series used "clanker" for battle droids), revived as an anti-AI meme in 2025.
sensitiveNote: Treated as a pretend slur for AI; some people worry it can be used to mock real groups through the same pattern.

definition: Looks-based put-down meaning unattractive or "ugly."
example: "He thinks he's chopped, but he's fine."
exampleTranslation: He thinks he looks bad, but he's fine.
context: Opposite of "mogging" culture; can hurt feelings. Use gently.
origin: From looksmaxxing forum language.
sensitiveNote: Appearance-based insult from looksmaxxing forums.

definition: Flamboyant or flashy; used jokingly, but often as a homophobic jab.
exampleTranslation: Not recommended as an insult.
context: Often aimed at boys to tease them about being "gay," which can be hurtful. Better to avoid.
origin: Older sense "lively and tangy" shifted into a gay-coded insult online.
sensitiveNote: Often used as a homophobic insult; recommend avoiding.

definition: A jokey way of describing a dramatic sideways look of disapproval.
example: "I gave him a bombastic side eye."
exampleTranslation: I gave him a dramatic disapproving look.
context: Often delivered with a pause and a squint. Comes from a viral clip.
origin: A 2023 TikTok line paired with a dramatic side-eye reaction.

term: it's so over / we're so back
definition: A dramatic swing between despair and hope, used for any small win or loss.
example: "I failed the quiz. It's so over." "I got extra credit. We're so back."
exampleTranslation: I failed the quiz and all is lost. Then I got extra credit and all is well.
context: Exaggerates ups and downs, borrowed from finance and sports memes.
origin: Crypto and sports online communities.

definition: Dominant, confident, leader-like; online memes treat it as the opposite of "beta."
example: "He acts so alpha with the group project."
exampleTranslation: He acts like the dominant leader on the group project.
context: Mostly joking now. Wolf pack "alpha" myth was debunked by scientists.
origin: From "alpha male" in animal behavior pop-science and the manosphere.
sensitiveNote: Tied to "manosphere" ideas that rank men; often cringe.

definition: An insult for a man seen as weak or submissive, the opposite of "alpha."
exampleTranslation: Don't be such a pushover.
context: Mostly a meme insult; discourages kindness. Some use it playfully.
origin: Manosphere ranking system.
sensitiveNote: Used to shame men for being gentle; better avoided.

definition: Slang for girls or women a speaker is interested in, from "hoes" via the pun "huzz."
exampleTranslation: He is out with the girls.
context: Originated as a mild respelling of a derogatory word, so can be disrespectful.
origin: Derived from a derogatory term for women, softened by respelling.
sensitiveNote: Euphemistic respelling of a derogatory term for women.

definition: A brain rot character: a wooden drum-bat that sings in a chant, inspired by a Ramadan pre-dawn "sahur" wake-up call in Indonesia.
example: "Tung tung tung tung sahur!" shouted my cousin.
exampleTranslation: My cousin shouted a meme chant.
context: Part of the "Italian brain rot" group, though it is Indonesian in origin. Not a mocking of Ramadan for most.
origin: Indonesian TikTok meme in 2025 that inspired the AI-generated "Italian brain rot" wave; "sahur" is the pre-dawn meal Muslims eat during Ramadan.
sensitiveNote: Sahur is a religious meal during Ramadan; some Muslim viewers find the meme disrespectful.

definition: A wave of AI-generated absurd characters with fake Italian-sounding names like "Tralalero Tralala."
example: "My little brother knows every Italian brain rot character."
exampleTranslation: My little brother knows every absurd AI character.
context: Quickly known among kids in 2025. Often considered nonsense overload.
origin: AI image and voice memes on TikTok in 2025.

definition: A tease starter, mocking someone who acts like they're more impressive than they are.
example: "Bro thinks he's a pro because he won once."
exampleTranslation: He acts like a pro because he won once.
context: Complete with any role: "bro thinks he's Messi."

definition: High praise meaning someone is that guy: the best and most impressive.
exampleTranslation: He scored twice. He's the best.
context: "I'm him" is a confident brag; "she's her" is the equivalent.
origin: Sports and streaming culture.

definition: A silly mash-up of "lowkey" and "genuinely" with a famous name inserted, used jokingly for "honestly."
exampleTranslation: Honestly, I love this game.
context: Seen in memes; many don't know the reference.
sensitiveNote: Blended with a real person's first name in some versions; origin is murky.

definition: A nonsense word meant to imitate a gunshot sound in the Pluh meme.
exampleTranslation: He made a silly shooting sound in the cafeteria.
context: From a Black meme ("pluh"); can refer to firearms, so teachers may discourage it.
origin: Spread on TikTok from a rapper's ad-libs.
sensitiveNote: Imitates a gunshot sound and may reference gun violence.

definition: A June 2023 TikTok trend where people drank a purple McDonald's milkshake and then acted as if something scary had happened.
example: "The Grimace shake videos were everywhere in 2023."
exampleTranslation: The purple milkshake videos were everywhere in 2023.
context: Mostly horror parodies; ended as a trend.
origin: McDonald's Grimace Birthday Meal (purple shake) went viral on TikTok in June 2023.

definition: A meme about a gathering with a "rizzler," often with exaggerated charm.
exampleTranslation: Welcome to the charm party.
context: Brain rot phrase, not a real event.

definition: The idea that you owe cool points after a lucky moment.
example: "I took the free fries, now I'm in aura debt."
exampleTranslation: I took the free fries and owe a favor.
context: Humor around aura points.

definition: The mix of nonsense slang (skibidi, gyatt, Ohio) used by Gen Alpha online.
example: "Her brain rot language confuses her parents."
exampleTranslation: Her slang confuses her parents.
context: Teachers and parents use this to describe slang overload.

definition: A joke "rule" such as "don't explain yourself" used to claim coolness.
exampleTranslation: Cool rule: never text first.
context: Sometimes ironic motivational posts.

definition: A joke about keeping up daily mewing, like a streak on an app.
exampleTranslation: I'm on a ten-day streak of posing for a sharp jaw.
context: Used to mock looks trends.

definition: A joke group of imaginary wise judges deciding the fate of something.
exampleTranslation: The judges decided.
context: Meme from sports or roleplay joking about secret decision makers.

definition: A mock-threat that someone has no hope.
example: "You forgot homework? It's over for you."
exampleTranslation: You forgot homework? You're done for.
context: Dramatic teasing.

definition: Slang for a hot dog.
example: "He ate three glizzies at the cookout."
exampleTranslation: He ate three hot dogs at the cookout.
context: Origin includes slang for a handgun in DC, so teens say it with wink.
origin: Washington, D.C. slang that spread widely online.
sensitiveNote: Local DC slang that can also refer to firearms.

definition: A joke for terrible or weird charm: "rizz" so bad it must be from Ohio.
example: "His pick-up line was straight Ohio rizz."
exampleTranslation: His pick-up line was weird.
context: Combines two memes.

definition: A viral 2024 catchphrase from a street interview; it refers to a sexual act, but is mostly used as a meme.
example: Teens quote it as a joke.
exampleTranslation: Teens repeat it as a joke.
context: Adults should not repeat it with kids; it's mature. Related to a 2024 viral interview.
origin: Viral TikTok street interview clip in 2024.
sensitiveNote: Refers to a sexual act; the viral interview made it well known.

definition: Calm and not bothered; in memes it means someone who acts unbothered.
exampleTranslation: He stayed calm after the loss.
context: Ordinary word used in memes as the "nonchalant dude" stereotype.

definition: A person with extreme charisma.
example: "He is a rizz god with the teacher."
exampleTranslation: He is very charming to the teacher.
context: Playful big title.

definition: Aura that is positive; a win in coolness.
exampleTranslation: That was cool.
context: Mix of "W" and aura.

definition: A meme where a haircut name is used as a joking answer to anything, like "Low taper fade, still massive."
exampleTranslation: He said the haircut meme.
context: Rule: say "low taper fade" to praise an unusual haircut meme.

definition: A template remarking that something is impressive or intense.
exampleTranslation: That is wild.
context: Substitute any noun.

definition: Cool, impressive; a respelling of "tough," often with a scrunched face emoji.
exampleTranslation: That drawing is awesome.
context: Also used ironically.

definition: Short for "opposition"; enemies or rivals. Gen Alpha uses it jokingly for people they dislike.
example: "Watch out for the opps at recess."
exampleTranslation: Watch out for the rivals at recess.
context: From rap and drill culture; originally violent.
origin: Hip-hop and drill music, then gaming.
sensitiveNote: Originates in gang and rap rivalries.

definition: Address for a younger or lesser person, jokingly.
exampleTranslation: This kid thinks he can win.
context: Teasing.

definition: A starter for describing a friend doing something silly: "bro is walking like a crab."
exampleTranslation: He is acting like a robot.
context: Casual narration.

definition: Stretched "ah" used as a modifier like "goofy ahh" or "tuff ahh."
exampleTranslation: That is a weird car.
context: A softened swearword stand-in.
sensitiveNote: Stand-in for a rude word.

definition: Abbreviation of "shut your beautiful ass up," used as a joking "be quiet."
exampleTranslation: Be quiet, I'm trying to focus.
context: Short form of a rude phrase.
sensitiveNote: Abbreviation of a profane phrase.

definition: A viral boy who became famous in 2025 for yelling "six seven" at a basketball game.
exampleTranslation: The viral boy went viral.
context: A real kid; be careful in making fun.
sensitiveNote: Refers to a real child; avoid targeting.

definition: A fake-nerdy "um, actually," often with the nerd emoji, used to joke about correcting someone.
exampleTranslation: Um, actually, that's not how it works.
context: Mocking pedantry.

definition: Friend term for a close buddy, as if they were a twin.
exampleTranslation: Friend, check this out.
context: Used among boys and girls.

definition: An exaggeratedly masculine meme figure; used to praise someone who seems perfect.
example: "He is the Gigachad of the team."
exampleTranslation: He is the ideal guy on the team.
context: From a viral black-and-white photo of a male model.
origin: From a 2017 photo series used as a meme, popularized on 4chan.

definition: Joke mindset of hustling endlessly in lone-wolf style.
exampleTranslation: Lone hustle: no sleep.
context: Parody of hustle culture.

definition: A meme dog in a sweater and jeans who stays calm; "just a chill guy."
exampleTranslation: Be a relaxed person.
context: Went viral in late 2024; also tied to a crypto token.
origin: Artist Philip Banks created the character; viral late 2024.

definition: A 2025 meme of an AI-style blue cat on a social app.
exampleTranslation: Everyone knows the blue cat meme.
context: Silly viral image.

definition: A chocolate bar with pistachio cream and crisp kataifi pastry that went viral on social media.
exampleTranslation: I tried a viral chocolate.
context: Food trend that peaked around 2024–2025.
origin: Created by Fix Dessert Chocolatier in Dubai; spread via TikTok.

definition: A toothy collectible monster toy by Pop Mart that became a huge fashion fad in 2025.
example: "She clipped a Labubu to her bag."
exampleTranslation: She clipped a trendy toy to her bag.
context: Popular as bag charms; knockoffs are called "Lafufu."
origin: Designed by artist Kasing Lung, sold by Pop Mart.

definition: An NFL-inspired dance that mimics a football receiver's high-knee moves.
exampleTranslation: Do the dance!
context: Popular among kids and players.
origin: Popularized by NFL player Justin Jefferson.

definition: A creepy internet legend of endless yellow office spaces.
exampleTranslation: I got lost in a creepy place.
context: Started as a 2019 post.
origin: 4chan post in 2019, expanded by creators like Kane Pixels.

definition: A catchphrase from a John Cena Chinese-language video meaning "ice cream."
exampleTranslation: Ice cream.
context: Meme from 2022 reference.

definition: An Italian brain rot character: a three-legged shark wearing blue sneakers.
exampleTranslation: The shark meme character is my favorite.
context: AI-made character.

definition: A brain rot figure with a cappuccino for a head.
exampleTranslation: The meme ballerina danced.
context: Italian brain rot character.

definition: A brain rot character that is a crocodile-shaped bomber plane.
exampleTranslation: The meme crocodile is funny.
context: AI-made character.

definition: A 2024 Incredibox music game mod with colorful characters that went viral with kids.
exampleTranslation: The music game is catchy.
context: Spawned fan mods and memes.

definition: Low-quality AI-generated content that floods the internet.
exampleTranslation: My feed is all junk content.
context: Merriam-Webster reportedly chose "slop" as its 2025 Word of the Year.

definition: Making software by telling an AI what you want in plain English and accepting its code.
example: "I did vibe coding for my game."
exampleTranslation: I made my game by prompting AI.
context: Term coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy in early 2025; Collins reportedly named it Word of the Year.
origin: Coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025.

definition: Joking short for "mental breakdown."
example: "I'm having a menty b about finals."
exampleTranslation: I'm having a meltdown about finals.
context: Said lightly for stress; avoid for real crises.

definition: A meme line from The Simpsons dares a person to say a catchphrase.
exampleTranslation: Go on, say it!
context: Meme of Bart in a movie scene.

definition: A baby pygmy hippo in a Thai zoo who became a viral meme in 2024.
exampleTranslation: The viral baby hippo is so cute.
context: Famous in September 2024.
origin: Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Thailand.

definition: Excellent or the best, often ironically.
exampleTranslation: This game is the best.
context: Used for anything amazing.

definition: A looksmaxxing term for deep-set eyes with an upward tilt seen as attractive.
exampleTranslation: He has sharp-looking eyes.
context: Looks forum jargon.
sensitiveNote: Appearance-ranking language.

definition: Angle of outer eye corners; looksmaxxers think a positive tilt is attractive.
exampleTranslation: Change your eye angle?
context: Body-focused jargon.
sensitiveNote: Appearance jargon.

definition: A 2025 Roblox game where players collect and steal meme characters.
exampleTranslation: I played the Roblox game.
context: Popular among kids.

definition: A 2025 Roblox farming game that went viral.
exampleTranslation: I played the game.
context: Hit game.

definition: Someone weirdly powerful or intense.
exampleTranslation: He is very intense.
context: Meme.

definition: A clownish silly person; used as a light insult.
exampleTranslation: The fool ran into the door.
context: Gets used with "L".

definition: Slang for fast rambling talk, as if it were a language.
exampleTranslation: He rambles.
context: Joke.
